text:
Shayne Gostisbehere is doing what Carolina keeps him around for. He has 16 points in 21 games, 8 of them on the power play, and at five on five the Hurricanes are taking 64% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) with him on the ice. That is one of the best numbers on the team, and it is 5.6 points better than Carolina manages without him.

Some of the points are luck, but less of it is his own. His shooting is right where it should be for a defenseman. The bigger tailwind is his teammates: Carolina has finished almost nine goals better than its chances with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he plays with strong teammates (91st percentile), which flatters raw on-ice numbers. Even with that, they had him driving play in the 86th percentile among defensemen.

The setup instincts are real. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 5.5 primary shot assists per 60. The assist pace may cool when the finishing around him does; the process underneath it looks sturdy.
